messages:
Arjun: Quick update — I ran a sensitivity sweep across A100/H100/L40S for: paged-attention (paged-flash variant) vs fused attention vs classic flash. Aim: seq len sweep (512, 1024, 2048), batch sweep (1, 8, 32, 64), measure tokens/s and KV-cache spill behavior.

Arjun: TL;DR: A100/H100 behave as expected. L40S starts hitting KV cache spill and host memcpy overhead beyond batch 32 at seq=2048 for the paged-flash path. Fused kernel is more stable on L40S but slightly lower peak throughput on H100.

Mika: Nice. Can you paste the exact bench command and the perf snippet?

Arjun: Sure — command I used (dockerized runtime, pinned GPUs):
```
./bench_runner 
  --model=gpt-style-7b 
  --kernel-selection=auto 
  --variants=paged-flash,fused,flash 
  --seq-lens=512,1024,2048 
  --batches=1,8,32,64 
  --kv-cache=true 
  --profile=perf_events,memcpy,meminfo 
  --devices=A100,H100,L40S
```

Arjun: Key perf table (tokens/s) from the run, cleaned up:
```
config                | A100 (peak) | H100 (peak) | L40S (peak)
paged-flash seq2048 b32 | 980k        | 1.05M       | 760k (spill)
fused seq2048 b32       | 920k        | 1.0M        | 810k
flash seq2048 b32       | 970k        | 1.04M       | 740k
paged-flash seq2048 b64 | 940k        | 1.02M       | 690k (heavy host memcpy)
```

Lucy: Hmm interesting. Did the profiler show where the extra time is on L40S?

Arjun: Yes — perf_events + nvprof trace: at high batch/seq the paged path triggers repeated KV-cache evictions/host writes. The L40S run shows a lot more `cudaMemcpyAsync` from device to host around the KV spill window. Looks like our paged eviction threshold is too aggressive on that memory config.

Sam: Did you hit OOM before spill or did we stay under device mem cap?

Arjun: Stayed under device mem cap for the forward pass, but KV cache reservation for large seq*batch grew and exceeded our in-GPU working set, so we started pushing pages to host. This isn't an OOM crash — it's more of a throughput regression because of PCIe/NVLink transfer frequency.

Mika: Could be a heuristic issue: batch-aware threshold should consider batch*seq peak, not just seq percent. We had a similar fix for tiled kernels last quarter.

Arjun: Agreed. I prototyped a simple heuristic: kv_page_eviction_threshold = max(0.6, 1.0 - 0.5 * (batch/64)) for the paged path. With that the L40S b64 seq2048 run still spilled but less frequently and tokens/s improved ~9%.

Lucy: Also worth checking host pinned memory usage. If memcpy is non-pinned it will be extra slow. Any difference in pinned allocations across devices?

Arjun: Good call — profiler shows pinned buffers were used for A100/H100, but on L40S the runtime path fell back to pageable for a couple of evicted pages. I think our allocator didn't reserve pinned staging buffers for the paged path on L40S in that docker image.

perf-bot: CI job #31207 finished for bench/sweep — artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/bench/1793456789/ (raw traces, flamegraphs).

Mika: Can you re-run L40S with: (1) kv heuristic loosened; (2) force pinned staging buffers; (3) try fused kernel with quantized weights? One short run each should show direction.

Arjun: Will run those tonight. Quick notes:
- Fused kernel + int8 quant gives ~12% lower peak on H100 vs float fused, but is much more tolerant to batch increases on L40S (no spills up to b64 seq2048 on test).
- Paged-flash is best for memory efficiency but sensitive to eviction heuristics + pinned buffer strategy.

Sam: If fused+quant is stable on L40S we can add it as a fallback policy in smart routing: prefer paged-flash for A100/H100, prefer fused-quant for L40S at high batch/seq.

Arjun: Yep. I'll upload a short reproducible script and a minimal flamegraph snapshot to the perf bucket. Also adding a perf note in the runtime PR describing the eviction heuristic change and pinned buffer fix.

Lucy: Thanks — also add a metric to the console: percent requests seeing KV spill and average memcpy time. We need visibility for customers.

Mika: Appreciate the numbers. If you can share the small script I'll run it on our L40S infra too.

Arjun: Script and artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/bench/1793456789/run_script.sh and flamegraphs under the same path. Will open a PR with heuristic + allocator change tomorrow. :ship:
